questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.keyword: Vendor Center New Vendor button
questions.text: A bookkeeper needs to create a new vendor record in QuickBooks Online. Which path leads directly to the New Vendor form?

answers.text: Left navigation bar → Expenses → Vendors sub-tab → New Vendor button at the top right.
+New → Vendor → New Vendor form.
Gear icon → Lists → Vendors → Add Vendor.
Left navigation bar → Sales → Customers → convert to Vendor.

explanations.a: The Student Guide states users navigate to the Vendor Center by clicking Expenses on the left navigation bar and selecting the Vendors sub-tab, then clicking the green New Vendor button at the top right.
explanations.b: +New opens transaction creation screens such as invoices and checks; it does not contain a New Vendor form path.
explanations.c: The gear icon Lists section contains list management options but does not have a direct Vendors entry described in the Student Guide.
explanations.d: The Sales → Customers path is for customer records; vendors are created through the Expenses → Vendors path.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.keyword: Vendor Credit expense purchase transaction types
questions.text: QuickBooks Online offers several types of expense and purchase transactions. Which of the following is one of the seven types listed in the Student Guide?

answers.text: Invoice
Vendor Credit
Sales Receipt
Receive Payment

explanations.a: Invoice is a sales-side transaction used to bill customers; it is not one of the expense/purchase transaction types.
explanations.b: Vendor Credit is one of the seven expense/purchase transaction types listed in the Student Guide, used to record refunds or credits received from vendors.
explanations.c: Sales Receipt is a customer-side transaction that records immediate payment; it is not an expense/purchase type.
explanations.d: Receive Payment is a customer-side transaction used to apply customer payments to open invoices; it is not an expense/purchase type.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.keyword: Pay Bill transaction relieve open bill
questions.text: A bookkeeper entered a vendor bill in QuickBooks Online and now needs to record the payment. Which transaction type must be used to properly close the open bill?

answers.text: A Check transaction written from the checking account.
An Expense transaction coded to Accounts Payable.
A Pay Bill transaction.
A bank deposit to the vendor's account.

explanations.a: Using a Check transaction to pay a bill that was already entered creates a double-recording error; Pay Bill is the correct transaction to relieve an open bill.
explanations.b: Using an Expense transaction to pay a previously entered bill overstates Accounts Payable and expenses; Pay Bill is required.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states that once a bill is created, a Pay Bill transaction must be used to record the payment and close the bill in QuickBooks Online.
explanations.d: Bank deposits record money received into the company, not money paid to vendors; this is not the correct transaction type.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.keyword: Purchase Orders Plus Advanced subscription activation
questions.text: A growing company wants to start sending purchase orders to vendors from within QuickBooks Online. What is the minimum subscription level required to activate the purchase order transaction?

answers.text: Simple Start
Essentials
Simple Start or Essentials — it is available at all levels.
Plus (or Advanced).

explanations.a: Simple Start does not include the purchase order feature; it is available only in Plus and Advanced.
explanations.b: Essentials does not include the purchase order feature; it is available only in Plus and Advanced.
explanations.c: Purchase orders are not available at all levels; Simple Start and Essentials do not include this feature.
explanations.d: The Student Guide states purchase orders can be activated in a QuickBooks Online Plus or Advanced company through the gear icon → Account and Settings → Expenses → Use purchase orders.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.keyword: Vendor Credit refund credit from vendor
questions.text: A vendor sends a credit memo for merchandise the company returned. Which QuickBooks Online transaction type is used to record this credit received from the vendor?

answers.text: Vendor Credit transaction form
Credit Memo
Refund Receipt
Bill Payment

explanations.a: The Student Guide states Vendor Credit transaction forms are used to record refunds or credits received from vendors.
explanations.b: Credit Memo is a customer-side transaction used to give customers a credit on an existing or future invoice; it is not used for vendor credits.
explanations.c: Refund Receipt is a customer-side transaction used when refunding money to a customer; it is not a vendor-side transaction.
explanations.d: Bill Payment records money paid to a vendor against an open bill; it is not used to record a credit received from a vendor.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.objective: 6.8 Category details vs. Item details sections
questions.keyword: Category details Item details two sections expense
questions.text: When entering an expense, check, or bill transaction in QuickBooks Online, the form is divided into two sections for recording what was purchased. What are these two sections called?

answers.text: Income section and Expense section.
Category details and Item details.
Account details and Product details.
General Ledger section and Product/Service section.

explanations.a: Income section and Expense section are not the names used for the two transaction entry sections in the Student Guide.
explanations.b: The Student Guide identifies the two sections on expense/purchase transaction screens as Category details (for general ledger account coding) and Item details (for product/service items).
explanations.c: Account details and Product details are not the section names used in the Student Guide for purchase transaction entry.
explanations.d: General Ledger section and Product/Service section are not the section names used in the Student Guide; the correct labels are Category details and Item details.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.objective: 6.3 Three ways to create purchase transactions
questions.keyword: +New left navigation create expense purchase
questions.text: According to the Student Guide, which of the following is one of the three main ways to create an expense or purchase transaction in QuickBooks Online?

answers.text: From the Banking Center by clicking a downloaded transaction and choosing Expense.
From the Chart of Accounts by selecting the checking account and clicking New Transaction.
Using +New at the top of the left navigation bar and selecting the transaction type.
From the Accounting tab by navigating to Transactions → New.

explanations.a: While downloaded banking transactions can be categorized as expenses, the Student Guide's three main creation methods do not specifically reference the Banking Center for this purpose.
explanations.b: Creating transactions from the Chart of Accounts is not listed among the three methods in the Student Guide.
explanations.c: The Student Guide lists using +New at the top of the left navigation bar as one of the three main ways to create expense and purchase transactions.
explanations.d: Navigating through the Accounting tab to create transactions is not described as one of the three methods in the Student Guide.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.keyword: Vendor Center Expenses Vendors sub-tab left navigation
questions.text: A bookkeeper wants to open the Vendor Center to review outstanding bills and vendor activity. Which navigation path leads to the Vendor Center?

answers.text: Gear icon → Lists → Vendors.
+New → Vendors → View All Vendors.
Left navigation bar → Accounting → Chart of Accounts → Vendor Accounts.
Left navigation bar → Expenses → Vendors sub-tab.

explanations.a: The gear icon Lists section does not contain a Vendor Center link as described in the Student Guide.
explanations.b: +New opens transaction screens; it does not provide a path to the Vendor Center list view.
explanations.c: The Accounting tab leads to Reconcile and Chart of Accounts, not the Vendor Center.
explanations.d: The Student Guide states clicking Expenses in the left navigation bar and then the Vendors sub-tab opens the Vendor Center listing all vendors.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.objective: 6.1 Creating a vendor on the fly
questions.keyword: Add New vendor on-the-fly Payee field during transaction
questions.text: While entering a bill, a bookkeeper types a vendor name that does not yet exist in QuickBooks Online. According to the Student Guide, what happens next and what options are presented?

answers.text: They are prompted to Add New; after specifying the record as a Vendor, they can choose to add details now or save the name to add details later.
QBO automatically creates a vendor record with the typed name and assigns it to an Uncategorized Vendor account.
The transaction cannot be saved until the vendor is first created in the Vendor Center.
The user must cancel the transaction, create the vendor, and then re-enter the transaction from the beginning.

explanations.a: The Student Guide states users will be prompted to Add New from the Payee/Vendor field drop-down; they specify it is a Vendor and can choose whether to add details now or save the name to add details later.
explanations.b: QBO does not automatically create vendor records silently; it prompts the user to confirm and classify the new name.
explanations.c: QBO does allow saving a new vendor name on the fly during transaction entry without first going to the Vendor Center.
explanations.d: Canceling and returning to the Vendor Center is unnecessary; QBO supports creating vendors on the fly during transaction entry.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.objective: 6.4 Expense vs. Check — choosing the right type
questions.keyword: Check transaction handwritten check date check number
questions.text: A company pays a supplier using a handwritten check drawn on the business checking account. Which transaction type is most appropriate, and what date and reference number should be used?

answers.text: Expense, since the payment left the checking account immediately and was not a credit card charge.
Check, using the date written on the check and the check number as the reference number.
Bill, to record the payable and then use Pay Bill when the check clears the bank.
Vendor Credit, because a check payment reduces the company's liability to the vendor.

explanations.a: While an Expense transaction can record checking account payments, the Student Guide specifically states that for check transactions, users should use the Check type with the date written on the check.
explanations.b: The Student Guide instructs users to use a Check transaction for handwritten checks, using the date written on the check and the check number as the reference number.
explanations.c: A Bill is used when a vendor invoice will be paid at a later date; for an already-written check, a Bill followed by Pay Bill adds unnecessary steps.
explanations.d: Vendor Credit records credits received from a vendor; it is not used to record a payment made to a vendor.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.keyword: bill paid with Check instead of Pay Bill double recording error
questions.text: A bookkeeper entered a vendor bill and then paid it using a Check transaction instead of a Pay Bill transaction. According to the Student Guide, what accounting problem does this create?

answers.text: The checking account is credited twice, overstating the cash balance.
The bill remains open and revenue is understated on the Profit and Loss.
Accounts Payable is overstated on the balance sheet and expenses are too high on the income statement.
The payment is recorded twice, creating a debit balance in Accounts Payable.

explanations.a: The checking account would be correctly reduced by the Check transaction, but the bill remains open, inflating Accounts Payable rather than the cash balance.
explanations.b: Revenue is not affected by a bill payment error; the problem affects Accounts Payable and expenses.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states that if a Check or Expense transaction is used to pay a bill that was already entered, Accounts Payable is overstated on the balance sheet and expenses are too high on the income statement.
explanations.d: Using a Check to pay a recorded bill creates an open bill in Accounts Payable (overstatement) and an extra expense debit, not a debit balance in Accounts Payable.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.keyword: purchase order non-posting no accounting transaction
questions.text: A purchasing manager creates a purchase order in QuickBooks Online for office supplies. What effect does creating the purchase order have on the company's accounting records?

answers.text: It debits the expense account and credits Accounts Payable for the anticipated purchase amount.
It creates a pending transaction in the bank feed awaiting a match to the vendor's invoice.
It increases the on-hand quantity of inventory items listed on the purchase order.
It does not post to the accounting records at all; a purchase order is a non-posting transaction.

explanations.a: A purchase order does not debit expenses or credit Accounts Payable; no accounting entry is made until the goods or bill is received.
explanations.b: Purchase orders do not create bank feed entries; bank feeds reflect actual cleared bank transactions.
explanations.c: Inventory quantities are updated only when a bill or receipt is processed for the items, not when the purchase order is created.
explanations.d: The Student Guide states that creating a purchase order does not create or post an accounting transaction to the company's books.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.objective: 6.6 Purchase Orders — converting to a Bill
questions.keyword: Copy to Bill purchase order received vendor profile
questions.text: After the goods on a purchase order are received, a bookkeeper needs to record the vendor's bill for those items. What is the correct process for converting the purchase order to a bill in QuickBooks Online?

answers.text: Open the vendor's profile, locate the open purchase order, and choose Copy to Bill — or open the PO directly and click Copy to Bill in the top right corner.
Go to +New → Bill and manually re-enter all the items from the purchase order on the new bill screen.
In the Banking Center, match the vendor's incoming bank transaction to the open purchase order.
In the Vendor Center money bar, click the Purchase Orders segment to auto-convert all open POs to bills simultaneously.

explanations.a: The Student Guide instructs users to open the vendor's profile, locate the open purchase order, and choose Copy to Bill from the Action column — or open the PO and click Copy to Bill in the top right corner — to create a bill with the PO details pre-populated.
explanations.b: Manually re-entering all PO items on a new bill bypasses the Copy to Bill workflow and does not link the bill to the original purchase order.
explanations.c: The Banking Center handles downloaded bank feed transactions, not purchase order to bill conversions.
explanations.d: There is no auto-convert-all function in the Vendor Center money bar for purchase orders; each PO is converted individually.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.objective: 6.7 Vendor Credit — how it is applied
questions.keyword: Vendor Credit applied Pay Bill reduces payment amount
questions.text: After recording a Vendor Credit for a returned item, how is the credit applied to reduce the amount owed to that vendor?

answers.text: QBO automatically deducts the credit from the next bill paid to that vendor with no further action required.
When paying bills for that vendor, the credit appears in the Pay Bill screen and can be selected to reduce the payment amount.
The user must manually create a journal entry debiting Accounts Payable and crediting the related expense account.
The credit can be applied only by creating a Credit Card Credit if the original purchase was charged to a credit card.

explanations.a: QBO does not automatically apply Vendor Credits to the next payment; the credit must be selected during the Pay Bill process.
explanations.b: When a Vendor Credit exists for a vendor, it is presented in the Pay Bill screen and can be checked to reduce the amount due on a bill payment.
explanations.c: Manual journal entries are not the standard method for applying Vendor Credits in QBO; the Pay Bill screen handles this.
explanations.d: A Credit Card Credit is used for credit card refunds specifically; Vendor Credits can be applied through Pay Bill regardless of the original payment method.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.keyword: Payment account field checking credit card Expense Check
questions.text: When creating an Expense or Check transaction in QuickBooks Online, which field indicates which bank or credit card account is being used to make the payment?

answers.text: The Payee field, which also determines which bank account to debit.
The lower Category details section, which links the transaction to the general ledger payment account.
The Payment account field, typically a checking or credit card account.
The Reference number field, which maps to the payment method and source account.

explanations.a: The Payee field identifies the vendor being paid; it does not specify the payment source account.
explanations.b: The Category details section is used to assign expense accounts or accounts payable, not to specify the payment source account.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states that for Expense or Check transactions, the appropriate Payment account (typically a checking or credit card account) must be selected.
explanations.d: The Reference number field holds the check number or vendor bill number; it does not identify the payment source account.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.keyword: partial bill payment enter amount Pay Bill screen
questions.text: A vendor bill totals $2,000 but the company can pay only $800 right now. How is a partial bill payment correctly recorded in QuickBooks Online?

answers.text: Record a Pay Bill for the full $2,000 and create a Vendor Credit for the $1,200 not yet paid.
Delete the original $2,000 bill and create a new bill for $800, then pay it in full.
Create an Expense transaction for $800 and leave the original bill open for the remaining balance.
In the Pay Bill screen, enter $800 in the payment amount field because it is less than the full amount outstanding.

explanations.a: A Vendor Credit represents a credit from the vendor, not an unpaid balance; it should not be used to reflect an amount still owed on a bill.
explanations.b: Deleting and recreating a bill loses the original transaction history and distorts the vendor's record.
explanations.c: Using an Expense to partially pay a bill creates the same double-recording problem as using a Check; Pay Bill is required.
explanations.d: The Student Guide states that if paying less than the full amount outstanding, the bookkeeper should enter the partial payment amount in the Pay Bill screen because it is less than the full amount due.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.keyword: purchase order custom transaction numbers own sequence
questions.text: In the Expenses tab of Account and Settings, purchase order custom transaction numbers can be enabled. What does activating this option allow the company to do?

answers.text: Assign their own numbering sequence to purchase orders rather than relying on QBO's automatic numbering.
Link purchase orders to specific bank accounts to track prepayment amounts.
Create purchase orders with embedded payment terms that automatically generate a bill on the due date.
Automatically match purchase order numbers to vendor invoice numbers during bill entry.

explanations.a: The Student Guide lists purchase order custom transaction numbers as a setting that allows the company to use its own PO numbering sequence rather than the system-assigned default.
explanations.b: Linking purchase orders to bank accounts for prepayment tracking is not described as a function of custom transaction numbers in the Student Guide.
explanations.c: Automatic bill generation from purchase orders on a due date is not described as a feature of custom transaction numbers.
explanations.d: Automatic matching of PO numbers to vendor invoice numbers is not described as a function of custom transaction numbers in the Student Guide.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.keyword: Vendor Credit +New vendor profile New transaction
questions.text: According to the Student Guide, which two methods can be used to create a Vendor Credit in QuickBooks Online?

answers.text: From the Vendor Center money bar by clicking the Credits segment, or from the Reconcile screen under Adjustments.
Using +New at the top of the left navigation bar, or from a vendor's profile by selecting New transaction → Vendor credit.
From the Banking Center by selecting a downloaded refund and choosing Vendor Credit, or from +New.
By opening the original bill and selecting Create Credit from the action menu at the top right of the bill screen.

explanations.a: The Vendor Center money bar does not have a Credits segment, and the Reconcile screen does not provide a Vendor Credit creation path.
explanations.b: The Student Guide lists two methods: clicking +New and selecting Vendor credit, or opening the Vendor Center, opening a vendor profile, selecting New transaction at the top right, and choosing Vendor credit.
explanations.c: Downloaded bank feed transactions are matched or categorized as expenses; they cannot directly create a Vendor Credit through the Banking Center.
explanations.d: Opening an existing bill and choosing Create Credit is not a method described in the Student Guide for creating a Vendor Credit.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.keyword: track expenses by customer billable Plus Advanced Expenses settings
questions.text: In the Expenses tab of Account and Settings, two related options control how the company tracks expenses in relation to customers. What are these two options according to the Student Guide?

answers.text: Require a customer name on all expense transactions, and auto-generate invoices for billable expenses each month.
Assign a department code to each expense, and split expenses between multiple customers automatically.
Track expenses and items by customer, and make expenses and items billable (available in Plus and Advanced only).
Display a customer column on the Expenses Center grid, and email expense summaries to customers automatically.

explanations.a: Requiring customer names on all expenses and auto-generating invoices monthly are not the two options described in the Student Guide.
explanations.b: Department codes and automatic expense splitting are not described as Expenses tab settings in the Student Guide.
explanations.c: The Student Guide lists 'Track expenses and items by customer' and 'Make expenses and items billable (Plus and Advanced only)' as two key options in the Expenses tab of Account and Settings.
explanations.d: Displaying a customer column and emailing expense summaries are not described as Account and Settings Expenses tab options in the Student Guide.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.keyword: money bar purchase orders accounts payable bills paid 30 days
questions.text: The money bar at the top of the Vendor Center displays colored segments that can be clicked to expand transaction lists. Which three categories of vendor activity are represented by those segments?

answers.text: Estimates, invoices, and customer payments.
Paychecks, payroll liabilities, and contractor payments.
Sales receipts, credit memos, and refund receipts.
Purchase orders, accounts payable (open bills), and bills paid within the last 30 days.

explanations.a: Estimates, invoices, and customer payments are sales-side transactions shown in the Customer Center money bar, not the Vendor Center.
explanations.b: Paychecks and payroll liabilities are managed in the Payroll center, not the Vendor Center money bar.
explanations.c: Sales receipts, credit memos, and refund receipts are customer-side transactions; the Vendor Center money bar reflects purchase-side activity.
explanations.d: The Student Guide states the Vendor Center money bar allows clicking colored segments to expand lists of purchase orders, accounts payable (open bills), and bills paid within the last 30 days.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.keyword: Print Checks +New transaction type vendor payment
questions.text: A bookkeeper needs to print physical checks for vendor payments directly from QuickBooks Online. According to the Student Guide, which statement accurately describes the Print Checks capability?

answers.text: Print Checks is available as a transaction option in +New, allowing checks to be printed after entering the payment details.
Checks can be printed only from the Pay Bill screen after a bill has been created and fully paid.
Printing checks requires exporting the transaction to a spreadsheet and using the bank's check printing portal.
Print Checks is available only for companies subscribed to QuickBooks Online Payroll.

explanations.a: The Student Guide lists Print Checks as one of the expense/purchase transaction types available in QBO, accessible through the +New menu.
explanations.b: Print Checks is available via +New independent of the Pay Bill workflow; it is not restricted to post-payment bill printing.
explanations.c: QBO has a built-in Print Checks feature; exporting to a spreadsheet or using a bank portal is not required.
explanations.d: Print Checks is a standard QBO feature unrelated to the Payroll subscription.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.keyword: Expense transaction date checking credit card statement
questions.text: A bookkeeper is entering an Expense transaction for a charge that appeared on the company credit card statement. According to the Student Guide, which date should be used for this Expense transaction?

answers.text: The date the vendor's invoice was issued by the supplier.
The date of the expense as it appears on the checking account or credit card statement.
The date the transaction is being entered into QuickBooks Online today.
The last day of the fiscal month in which the expense occurred.

explanations.a: The vendor's invoice date is used when recording a Bill transaction, not an Expense; the Expense date should reflect when it cleared the account.
explanations.b: The Student Guide instructs users to use the date of the expense from the checking or credit card account statement when entering an Expense transaction.
explanations.c: Using today's data entry date rather than the statement date would misstate the period in which the expense occurred.
explanations.d: Using the last day of the fiscal month is not the guidance given in the Student Guide for Expense transaction dates.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.keyword: default date previous transaction last date used pre-fill
questions.text: When opening a new Expense, Check, or Bill transaction screen in QuickBooks Online, the date field is pre-filled automatically. What is the default date that QBO uses?

answers.text: Today's date is always inserted automatically when any new transaction screen opens.
The first day of the current accounting period is inserted as the default date.
The last date used on the previous transaction entered is pre-filled as the default date.
No date is pre-filled; the user must manually enter the date before the transaction can be saved.

explanations.a: QBO does not always insert today's date; the default date is the last date used on the previous transaction.
explanations.b: The first day of the current accounting period is not the default date behavior described in the Student Guide.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states the default date in a new transaction screen is the last date used on the previous transaction entered.
explanations.d: The date field is pre-filled automatically in QBO; it does not remain blank requiring manual entry.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.objective: 6.6 Purchase Orders — backorder handling when converting to bill
questions.keyword: backorder quantity received less than PO copy to bill
questions.text: A purchase order is converted to a bill after goods arrive, but only 7 of the 10 ordered units were delivered. According to the Student Guide, how should the bookkeeper handle the remaining 3 units on the bill?

answers.text: Create the bill for the full 10-unit quantity and generate a Vendor Credit for the 3 undelivered units.
Delete the original PO and create two separate bills — one for the 7 received units and one for the 3 backordered units.
Accept the full 10-unit quantity on the bill and create an inventory quantity adjustment to reduce the count by 3.
Change the quantity on the bill to 7 (the number received); the remaining 3 units stay on the original purchase order as backordered.

explanations.a: Creating a Vendor Credit for undelivered units misrepresents the transaction; the correct approach is to adjust the bill quantity to what was actually received.
explanations.b: Deleting the PO and splitting into two bills loses the link to the original purchase order and adds unnecessary complexity.
explanations.c: Accepting the full 10 units when only 7 were received overstates inventory and the bill amount; the quantity should be corrected on the bill.
explanations.d: The Student Guide states that if using Item details and fewer units were received than ordered, the quantity on the bill can be changed to the number actually received, with the remainder treated as backordered on the original purchase order.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.objective: 6.7 Credit Card Credit purpose and usage
questions.keyword: Credit Card Credit original purchase credit card refund
questions.text: A company purchased office supplies on its business credit card and later returned the items. The vendor issued a credit back to the card. Which transaction type in QuickBooks Online should be used to record this credit?

answers.text: Credit Card Credit, since the original purchase was made on a credit card and the refund is being returned to the card.
Vendor Credit, regardless of the original payment method, since the credit originates from the vendor.
A negative Expense transaction coded to the same expense account as the original purchase.
A Deposit transaction with the refund coded to the original expense account to reduce the expense balance.

explanations.a: The Student Guide lists Credit Card Credit as one of the expense/purchase transaction types, used when a credit is returned to a credit card account following a purchase originally made on that card.
explanations.b: A Vendor Credit is used when the credit does not return to a specific payment method (such as store credit or a check); when the refund goes back to a credit card, Credit Card Credit is the appropriate type.
explanations.c: Negative Expense transactions are not the standard QBO method for recording credit card refunds; Credit Card Credit is the correct transaction type.
explanations.d: A Deposit transaction is used for money received into a bank account; a credit card refund is recorded with a Credit Card Credit, not a deposit.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.keyword: Track payments 1099 reporting vendor record any subscription
questions.text: A business needs to issue Form 1099-MISC to certain independent contractors at year-end. According to the Student Guide, which step during vendor setup enables payment tracking for 1099 reporting?

answers.text: Assign the vendor to a '1099 Contractor' product/service item so QBO automatically tracks all eligible payments.
In the vendor record, check the box to Track payments for 1099 reporting; this option is available at any QBO subscription level.
Go to Account and Settings → Expenses and enable 1099 tracking for all vendors simultaneously as a global setting.
In the Vendor Center, click Prepare 1099s to designate 1099 vendors before entering any transactions.

explanations.a: There is no '1099 Contractor' product/service item in QBO; 1099 tracking is enabled via a checkbox in the vendor record itself.
explanations.b: The Student Guide states the vendor record includes an option to click the box to Track payments for 1099 reporting, and that this is available with any QBO subscription level.
explanations.c: Enabling 1099 tracking globally in Account and Settings is not described in the Student Guide; it is configured at the individual vendor record level.
explanations.d: The Prepare 1099s button in the Vendor Center is used at year-end to process forms, not to designate vendors for tracking before transactions are entered.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.keyword: Billing rate field vendor record billable time tracking
questions.text: A company uses billable time tracking and needs to record a subcontractor's hourly billing rate in their vendor record. According to the Student Guide, where is the billing rate for a vendor entered?

answers.text: In the Products and Services list, by creating a Service item with the subcontractor's rate as the default price.
In the Time Tracking settings under the Advanced tab of Account and Settings.
Directly in the vendor record during vendor setup, in the Billing rate field.
In the weekly timesheet entry for the subcontractor, entered manually each pay period.

explanations.a: A Service item can hold a rate but is not the same as the vendor-level Billing rate field described for subcontractor tracking in the Student Guide.
explanations.b: The Advanced tab of Account and Settings contains time tracking options but does not store individual vendor billing rates.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states that if tracking billable time, the Billing rate is entered in the vendor record during vendor setup.
explanations.d: Entering the billing rate manually in each timesheet each pay period is inefficient and not the approach described; the rate is stored once in the vendor record.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.objective: 6.6 Purchase Orders — link between PO and resulting bill
questions.keyword: PO bill linked original PO items received status
questions.text: After a purchase order is converted to a bill in QuickBooks Online, what is the ongoing relationship between the two documents?

answers.text: The original purchase order is automatically deleted and fully replaced by the new bill.
The original purchase order is archived as a read-only record and the bill is an entirely independent new document.
The purchase order and bill share the same transaction ID, making them a single combined record.
The bill and the purchase order are linked to each other; opening the original purchase order shows that the items on it have been received.

explanations.a: The original purchase order is not deleted when converted to a bill; it remains and is linked to the new bill.
explanations.b: The purchase order is not simply archived as independent read-only; it is actively linked to the resulting bill, showing item receipt status.
explanations.c: The bill and purchase order are separate documents with their own transaction IDs; they are linked but not merged into a single record.
explanations.d: The Student Guide states the new bill and the pre-existing purchase order are linked to each other, and opening the original purchase order shows that the items have been received.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.objective: 6.6 Purchase Orders — default messages setting location
questions.keyword: default message purchase order Expenses tab Account and Settings
questions.text: A procurement manager wants to set a standard default message that automatically appears on all purchase orders sent to vendors. According to the Student Guide, where is this default message configured?

answers.text: In the Expenses tab of Account and Settings, in the purchase order settings section.
In the Sales tab of Account and Settings, under the Messages section.
In the Advanced tab of Account and Settings, within the automation features.
Directly on each individual purchase order in the Message to vendor field, with no way to save a global default.

explanations.a: The Student Guide lists 'Default messages on purchase orders' as one of the settings configured in the Expenses tab of Account and Settings.
explanations.b: The Sales tab Messages section controls default email and messaging for sales forms such as invoices; purchase order messages are in the Expenses tab.
explanations.c: The Advanced tab automation features cover pre-fill, credit application, and similar options; purchase order message defaults are not located there.
explanations.d: While individual purchase orders have a message field, the Student Guide describes a global default message setting in Account and Settings for purchase orders.

questions.name: Vendors & Purchase Transactions
questions.objective: 6.1 Vendor record — Business ID number field
questions.keyword: Business ID number vendor record tax identification
questions.text: When creating a vendor record in QuickBooks Online, a field is available to store the vendor's tax identification number. What is this field called in QBO according to the Student Guide?

answers.text: EIN field, which stores the Employer Identification Number automatically transferred to Form 1099 at year-end.
Business ID number, a field in the vendor record where the vendor's tax ID can be stored for reference.
Tax ID field, which is automatically transferred to Form 1099-MISC at year-end when 1099 tracking is enabled.
SSN/EIN field, which requires the user to specify whether the number is a Social Security Number or EIN.

explanations.a: The field is called Business ID number in the Student Guide, not EIN field; and its automatic transfer to 1099 forms is not described as the field's function.
explanations.b: The Student Guide states vendors can have their Business ID number stored in the vendor record as a reference field during vendor setup.
explanations.c: Tax ID field is not the label used in the Student Guide; the correct label is Business ID number.
explanations.d: SSN/EIN with a type selector is not the field description provided in the Student Guide; it is simply called Business ID number.
